providers.name: Close
providers.tag: For a team that spends its day calling
providers.fit: Calling, email and follow-up in the same CRM.
providers.calling: Native calling. Growth adds a power dialer; Scale adds predictive.
providers.catch: Power dialing starts on Growth. Calls and numbers still cost extra.
providers.price: USD 99/user/month billed annually, or USD 109 on monthly billing.
providers.costNote: Calling, phone numbers and optional usage are extra.
providers.strength: Growth includes a power dialer and Workflows, with contact history, the call queue and follow-up in one system.
providers.drawback: Essentials excludes Workflows and the power dialer. Growth has additional calling and phone number charges. Check whether the import covers historical calls, notes and tasks as well as contacts.
providers.verdict: Start with Growth if a small team needs to call and manage follow-up inside its CRM. Check whether predictive dialing justifies the upgrade to Scale, and include migration work in the switching cost.
providers.check: Bring a shared company number, a scheduled callback and old call history. Confirm the queue, record matching and import result.

providers.name: HubSpot Sales Hub
providers.tag: When sales shares the wider customer record
providers.fit: Sales working with marketing and other teams in HubSpot.
providers.calling: Native calling with account-level limits. Sequences need an eligible paid seat and plan.
providers.catch: Professional has USD 1,500 onboarding. Its 3,000 calling minutes are shared, not per rep.
providers.price: USD 90/seat/month paid annually, or USD 100 paid monthly with an annual commitment.
providers.costNote: Add USD 1,500 one-time onboarding. 3,000 calling minutes/account/month are shared; extra usage can cost more.
providers.strength: A sensible shortlist when sales needs the same contact history as marketing and the rest of the business. Professional includes sequences and broader automation. Keeping those teams on connected records can matter more than the lowest seat price.
providers.drawback: The free or discounted Starter headline does not price a Professional outbound workflow. Onboarding adds USD 1,500. Calling minutes are pooled across the account, and country support and extra capacity need checking.
providers.verdict: Keep it on the list if your business already runs on HubSpot. For a small calling team, compare Professional's first-year cost with systems built around a call queue and callbacks.
providers.check: Ask for the first-year bill, assigned Sales Seats, shared minutes and exact sequence rules. Test a reply, a booked meeting and a reschedule. Your existing bundle may change the quote.

providers.name: Pipedrive
providers.tag: A clear pipeline with your choice of calling app
providers.fit: Teams that want pipeline visibility and structured follow-up.
providers.calling: Web calling uses a Marketplace app. Mobile calling has its own supported routes.
providers.catch: Budget for the calling app and check what actually gets logged.
providers.price: USD 39/seat/month billed annually, or USD 49 on monthly billing.
providers.costNote: Separate calling software and usage are not included.
providers.strength: Growth adds email sync, automations and follow-up sequences to a visual pipeline. It fits teams that want to see each deal's next action and are comfortable choosing the phone system separately.
providers.drawback: Pipedrive's web calling requires a connected phone app. Add its subscription and usage charges to the CRM price, and check what the integration logs.
providers.verdict: Choose it when pipeline visibility is the priority. For cold calling, check that your selected app logs notes, records outcomes and schedules callbacks in Pipedrive.
providers.check: Test Pipedrive with the calling app your team plans to use. Make a callback, update an existing person and import two people sharing a switchboard.

providers.name: Freshsales
providers.tag: Calling and follow-up at a lower subscription price
providers.fit: Small teams comparing built-in phone and sales sequences.
providers.calling: Built-in phone, funded by phone credits. Confirm power-dialer eligibility.
providers.catch: Freshsales, Freshsales Suite and Freshcaller are different products and configurations.
providers.price: USD 39/user/month billed annually, or USD 47 on monthly billing.
providers.costNote: Phone numbers and calling credits are extra. Confirm the exact phone package.
providers.strength: Pro includes sales sequences with email, call and task steps, alongside built-in phone. That is a relevant starting point when a small team wants organised follow-up without the subscription price of some larger platforms.
providers.drawback: Phone credits are separate. The power-dialer help page limits access to eligible Freshsales Suite accounts, so confirm eligibility for the product and plan in your quote.
providers.verdict: Start with Freshsales Pro when you need built-in calling and sequences at a lower subscription cost. Confirm which phone features and credits the quote includes.
providers.check: Confirm power-dialer access, number availability and usage charges. Pro currently lists ten sequences per user. Run the same callback and import checks you would run on the more expensive CRMs.

providers.name: Zoho CRM
providers.tag: For a team prepared to configure the workflow
providers.fit: Budget-conscious teams, especially those already using Zoho.
providers.calling: Confirm the telephony service or Zoho Voice configuration and its charges.
providers.catch: The CRM seat price does not establish the cost of your phone system or power dialer.
providers.price: USD 14/user/month billed annually, or USD 20 on monthly billing.
providers.costNote: Phone service, numbers, usage and any advanced dialer are separate buying checks.
providers.strength: Standard includes Cadences for follow-up. It suits teams seeking a lower subscription price or already working with other Zoho products.
providers.drawback: A connected phone service has its own costs and behaviour. Cadence limits vary by edition, and Professional adds process controls. Include time to configure the calling queue and rules for ending follow-up.
providers.verdict: Consider it if you already use Zoho or can assign someone to configure the fields, calling queues and follow-up rules. Include the phone system and setup work when comparing costs.
providers.check: Use full CRM user seats for calling reps. Show how a reply or stop request ends follow-up, and where a callback lands. Confirm the calling integration and account-specific rollout before committing.

providers.name: Salesforce
providers.tag: When the wider sales operation needs it
providers.fit: Teams with established Salesforce processes or deeper configuration needs.
providers.calling: The calling and sales-cadence setup depends on edition and connected products.
providers.catch: Starter's USD 25 headline is not a quote for a complete SDR workflow.
providers.price: Starter Suite: USD 25/user/month, monthly or annual billing. Confirm the edition and quote for calling and cadences.
providers.costNote: We have not established a complete calling configuration. Ask for the exact edition, phone service and follow-up tools.
providers.strength: Salesforce offers extensive configuration and reporting options across a wider sales operation. If the company already uses it, keeping account ownership, opportunities and handoffs in that system may be more useful than introducing another CRM.
providers.drawback: The current pricing page and Sales Engagement documentation use different edition labels. Ask Salesforce to confirm which edition and add-ons support your calling and cadence setup. Get the configuration and implementation responsibilities in writing.
providers.verdict: Use it when the wider business needs its configuration and reporting or already runs on Salesforce. A small team focused on calling and booking meetings should compare the simpler options first.
providers.check: Have the rep demonstrate the call queue, cadences, meeting handoff and reporting on the quoted edition. Confirm who will administer it and which charges sit outside the quote.

providers.name: monday CRM
providers.fit: Teams coordinating sales tasks and handoffs through a visual workspace.
providers.calling: Native Smart Call runs through the mobile app. It is not a browser power dialer.
providers.catch: Minimum three paid seats. Smart Call usage consumes AI credits.
providers.price: USD 28/seat/month billed annually, or USD 41 on monthly billing. Minimum three seats, then seat buckets.
providers.costNote: One user still pays for three seats. Calling consumes credits; other apps can add fees.
providers.strength: A visual workspace for leads, deals and team handoffs, with sequences on Pro. Smart Call adds mobile calling and logged call history.
providers.drawback: Smart Call currently has no browser calling or power dialer. Connected minutes consume five AI credits each, and plans start at three paid seats. Confirm the cost of those credits and the setup required for a desktop calling queue.
providers.verdict: Choose it for visual coordination and mobile calls. Reps power dialing from laptops need a separate desktop calling setup.
providers.check: Test an incoming callback as well as an outgoing call. With an external verified caller ID, return calls go to that external number and bypass monday's logging.

checks.title: Import without merging the wrong people.
checks.text: Use a small sample with two contacts sharing a company number. Keep both people, their number types and the existing record IDs.

checks.title: Log the call and see the next action.
checks.text: Record a voicemail, a wrong number and a conversation separately. Check that the next rep can understand what happened.

checks.title: Find the promised callback.
checks.text: Set a callback with a date, time zone and owner. It should appear when due and stay out of the generic unworked queue.

checks.title: Stop follow-up when it should stop.
checks.text: Use a test record for a stop request or reply. Confirm that the dialing queue, sequence and future tasks all reflect the change.

checks.title: Book, reschedule and hand over a meeting.
checks.text: Use a controlled test record. Keep qualification notes and the new meeting time together, without duplicate deals or stale reminders.

checks.title: Hand the record to another rep.
checks.text: Change the owner, check the history and next task, then inspect an export. Find out what happens to notes and recordings if you leave.

faqs.q: What is the best CRM for cold calling?
faqs.a: Choose Close Growth for a native power dialer and automated follow-up. Compare Freshsales Pro for built-in phone and sequences; check power-dialer access separately. Keep your existing HubSpot, Pipedrive, Zoho or Salesforce setup if it already handles records and connects to the dialer you need.

faqs.q: Which CRM is best for a small outbound sales team?
faqs.a: Shortlist around the work: Close for calling in the CRM; Pipedrive for a visual pipeline with a separate calling app; Freshsales or Zoho when subscription cost matters. Include HubSpot or Salesforce when the wider business already uses it. For one person considering monday CRM, account for its three-seat minimum. Trial the callback and follow-up workflow before paying annually.

faqs.q: Does a CRM with calling include a power dialer?
faqs.a: Not necessarily. Click-to-call, mobile calling and a power dialer are different workflows. Close places power dialing on Growth. Pipedrive web calling uses a connected app. monday Smart Call is mobile-based and currently lacks power dialing. Ask the vendor to show the mode on the exact plan you are buying.

faqs.q: Can I use Apollo instead of a CRM?
faqs.a: Apollo supports deals, tasks and pipeline reporting as well as prospecting and outreach. It may cover a small team's requirements. Before buying another CRM, check ownership, history, follow-up, reporting and the handoff you need. If you connect a CRM, decide which system owns each field and stage, and test the sync.

faqs.q: How much does a CRM for cold calling cost?
faqs.a: Separate the CRM subscription from the calling setup. This guide shows selected annual-plan subscriptions for one, three and five users. Phone usage, numbers, dialer apps, onboarding and AI credits can be additional costs. HubSpot Professional has required onboarding, and monday CRM has a minimum seat purchase. Salesforce's configured calling cost requires an edition-specific quote.

faqs.q: Do I need to change my CRM before hiring a cold calling agency?
faqs.a: Not automatically. First agree on account ownership, required fields, suppression rules, activity reporting and meeting handoff. Discuss the access or import process with the agency. CallTeam can review that workflow with you; an exact integration should be confirmed for the campaign rather than assumed.

faqs.q: Will an AI CRM fix missed follow-ups?
faqs.a: It can help create tasks or summarise activity, but somebody still needs to own the rules. Test whether a callback keeps its agreed time, a reply ends the correct sequence, and a stop request reaches every calling queue. A generated summary is useful only if it is accurate and the next action reaches the right person.
